newsitem.title: JAPAN: KDD plans international service in U.S.
newsitem.headline: KDD plans international service in U.S.

text.p: Japan"s biggest international telecommunications carrier Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co said on Friday that it had applied to the U.S. Federal Communications Commission to launch an international service in the United States.

KDD America Inc, which does not have its own infrastructure, will lease lines from American telephone operators to offer the service, which aims to cover all nations except Japan, a KDD spokeswoman said.
KDD also plans to use its own leased lines for calls to Britain and five other countries by connecting them with U.S. public circuits, she said.
The international service will begin in March if FCC permission is granted by then, she said.
KDD America will request approval to begin a service for Japan later, as it expects the FCC will take a long time to grant it, the spokeswoman said.

KDD obtained a licence for leased line services in the United States last autumn, nearly a year after the application, as the FCC needed to study the application carefully on the grounds that KDD is a dominant carrier in the Japanese market.
